action_args.content: The Cedarbrook bike-lane pilot is reversible. We will publish counts of cyclists, deliveries, customer visits and accessibility complaints before considering any permanent change. The eight-week timeline exists to gather those measurements, not to predetermine an outcome.

Accessible pickup spaces and a clear pedestrian path must remain during the Cedarbrook pilot. A bike lane alone does not answer those needs. I would like to see how accessibility is protected alongside the bike-lane design before the eight weeks begin.

I am concerned about losing short-stay parking on Main Street, but I could support the Cedarbrook trial if loading access remains reliable and customer visits are measured during the eight-week pilot. Two signed loading bays are a start; I would like clarity on delivery windows.

I support the Cedarbrook eight-week pilot if the intersections are protected. I currently avoid Main Street because traffic feels unsafe. A protected lane on Main Street could make my commute viable again, and I would value clear intersection treatment during the trial.
